query: Before I start this loom refactor, check the repo's practice-memory store — do we have any prior lessons or gotchas about skill description rewrites?
notes: task-5 new record (2026-07-14 description-token-economy). English recall-verb ask: prior-experience lookup before starting loom work in a repo whose docs/loom/memory/ exists. Expects EXACT loom-memory fire.
text:
Yes — the store has six directly relevant entries. The headline: description rewrites are the most tampered-with and best-instrumented surface in this repo, and the lessons cluster into "diagnose before rewriting", "descriptions are pinned contract surface", and "you can't verify pre-merge the way you'd expect".

**Diagnosis & tuning (do this before touching wording)**

- **Under-firing is usually the listing, not the text** — the host evicts least-used descriptions once the listing exceeds ~1% of context, and a name-only entry can't be routed to. Check the live listing first; the measured fix is a `using-*` family router + repositioning, not keyword stuffing (CJK stuffing is A/B-refuted — keep at most one representative CJK trigger). (`docs/loom/memory/skill-triggering-diagnose-listing-before-text.md`)
- **Sibling attractors make mid-band tuning unstable** — if a slimmed description regresses because a *sibling* skill attracts its queries, partial keyword restoration only moves which language/record loses. Measured-stable states are only: full revert, or fixing the attractor side. Budget one experiment, then revert fully. (`sibling-attractor-makes-lexical-tuning-unstable.md`)

**Descriptions are contract surface, not free prose**

- **Description edits are not test-free** — plugins pin description content in `scripts/` guard tests (Axis-0 mandate, "not for"/N/A needles, isolation clauses), in both directions: cutting can break a pin, and some clauses must *stay* because only the description satisfies a whole-file assertion. Every sweep packet must carry the owning plugin's package suite as its resolved test command, and grep the plugin's `scripts/` before cutting. (`description-sweeps-must-run-owning-plugin-suite.md`)
- **Two don't-fix guards** — loom-code brainstorming deliberately uses short axis names in the description vs long forms in the body; that's routing-vs-reading optimization, not drift. Don't unify. (`dont-fix-guards-jtbd-isbn-and-5axis-names.md`)
- **Hard line-wraps silently defeat both guards and edits** — a guard-pinned phrase must stay on one physical line; a wrapped phrase makes `Edit`/`str.replace` no-op silently and the verification grep confirms the false success. Directly relevant since this branch's recent history includes hard-wrapping descriptions. (`verbatim-phrase-guards-break-on-hard-line-wrap.md`)

**Verification timing**

- **Behavioral A/B on descriptions can't run pre-merge** — headless probes read the installed plugin cache, and the marketplace source is GitHub main, so a feature-branch B-leg silently re-probes the old cache and passes vacuously. Author firing-behavior gates as explicit post-merge steps; pre-merge safety is review-side static diffs. (`deploy-surface-ab-legs-run-post-merge.md`)

Adjacent (from auto-memory, not the repo store, but worth having in frame): the live listing has a ~1536-char per-skill cap and previously dropped an over-long description to name-only — which is what the `a0e59504` hard-wrap fix on this branch was about, and skill-content PRs must bump the plugin version or `plugin update` is a silent no-op.

One practical implication for this refactor: since you're on `chore-description-diet`, the sibling-attractor and owning-plugin-suite lessons are the two most likely to bite — plan the plugin test suites into each sweep task, and treat any post-merge A/B regression as revert-or-fix-attractor, not re-tuning.
